document_note: Format example for the benchmark fixture. It is not a complete review and is not evidence that the skill's editorial judgment has been validated.

findings.title: 12 March is both Tuesday and Wednesday
findings.description: The narration dates the storm to Tuesday, 12 March, and later to Wednesday, 12 March.

evidence.quote: The rain reached the coast on Tuesday, 12 March, and turned the lane to the inn into a strip of black mud.
On Wednesday, 12 March, the rain had not stopped.

findings.explanation: Both sentences are narrator statements about the same calendar date. No later passage corrects the weekday.
findings.narrative_impact: A reader who is tracking the storm cannot tell which day the arrival and the letter occupy.
findings.suggested_intervention: Make the weekday of 12 March consistent, or mark one statement as a character's mistake.

findings.title: The attic bargain holds
findings.description: Elena and Tomas each want something, and the scene ends without restating the price.

evidence.quote: Elena set her wet gloves on the ledger and waited.

findings.explanation: The exchange has a want, an obstacle, and a turn. The narration does not explain the bargain again after the action has shown it.
findings.narrative_impact: The scene can stay as written. Changing it would discard a clear piece of pressure.
